summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted for a deceased donor liver transplant due to alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis with hepatocellular carcinoma. The transplant surgery was complicated by significant intraoperative bleeding requiring multiple transfusions and two re-explorations for hemorrhage control. He remained intubated in the ICU for several days, with gradual improvement in respiratory and renal function. His liver enzymes normalized over time, and a biopsy of the allograft showed only mild preservation injury without rejection. He developed steroid-induced hyperglycemia, managed with insulin, and was monitored for potential infection due to the donor's coagulase-negative staph. He progressed well with physical therapy, had abdominal drains removed, and was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation on postoperative day 13 with a stable condition and a full regimen of immunosuppressive and prophylactic medications.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Acute respiratory failure following trauma and surgery
Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, not stated as uncontrolled, or unspecified
Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
